Stillwater is a living aquarium: a planted tank of tall grass leaning in a slow current, a driftwood branch furred with moss, dark boulders and pebbles on pale sand, sixteen silver tetras and two crabs. Light ripples across the sand from the surface above. There is nothing to win; it is there to be looked at.

Click the glass near a fish to startle it. It darts away from your finger, then settles into a new loop where it landed. The crabs shuffle a little sideways. Each tap makes a soft knock on the glass.

Space (or Pause in the menu) stops the tank exactly where it is. A paused tank does no work at all, and Resume continues from the same moment. The tank also stops whenever another game or the shelf is in front.

Detail (D) chooses the size of the tank's pixels: Fine is sharper, Light is gentlest on an older or busy computer, Balanced sits between. Whatever the detail, the tank measures what it costs and slows its swimming and swaying a little rather than take more than its share of the processor, and it slows further while another window is in front.

With Reduced Motion on, the grass and the rippling light hold still; the fish keep swimming.

The scene is Riverscape from Desktop Habitats by Chase Lean (MIT), carried over from the Stillwater aquarium. The sand, rock and wood surfaces are Poly Haven textures (CC0). Everything is drawn by the processor; no graphics card is needed.
